champion: Vascular Tumor of the Thyroid with Metastasis
ordered_diagnoses: Vascular Tumor of the Thyroid with Metastasis
Supratentorial Hemangioblastoma at the Anterior Skull Base

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction with highly vascularized mass
salient_findings: Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Considerable uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy regarding rib and vertebral lesions
key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction
Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Sinonasal tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy
Serum thyroglobulin was significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results confirmed VTC metastasis in the costal and sinonasal tumor biopsies

raw.champion: Vascular Tumor of the Thyroid with Metastasis
raw.rationale: The combination of a highly vascularized mass in the nasal cavities, elevated serum thyroglobulin, and biopsy-confirmed VTC metastasis in both costal and sinonasal tumor biopsies supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Encapsulated Sinonasal Schwannoma
rejected.why: Lack of encapsulation description and absence of typical schwannoma features in imaging

rejected.label: Supratentorial Hemangioblastoma at the Anterior Skull Base
rejected.why: No mention of cerebellar or spinal hemangioblastoma typical locations, and the presence of thyroid and distant metastases

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not align with the typical multifocal and multisystem involvement of LCH

rejected.label: Hereditary Angioedema
rejected.why: The chronic and progressive nature of the symptoms, along with the presence of a mass and elevated thyroglobulin, do not support this diagnosis
